summary: a procfs mounted with ProcSubset=pid (or an equivalent restricted view) makes every Linux allowlist key read ENOENT, reading as 11 clean 'absent' rows instead of a degraded read
trigger: an operator drop-in ProcSubset=pid, or a container/chroot with no /proc/sys tree
classification_rationale: the binding contract (definitive OS absence vs a degraded/incomplete read) cannot distinguish these two causes today -- corrected: impact I3 + exposure E4/E5 derives HIGH/BLOCKING per the shared preamble, not the originally-recorded MEDIUM/SHOULD. Fixed by an all-eleven-ENOENT canary in collect_linux_posture (system_hardening_parsers.hpp): each key still reads its own absent/unreadable truth; only when ALL 11 Linux allowlist keys read ENOENT does the accumulator add one proc_sys:not_visible token, downgrading the run to CONSTRAINED. Regression test added (test_system_hardening_parsers.cpp); a false-positive guard test confirms a mostly-present host with a few legitimately-absent keys never trips the canary.

trigger: the doc generator's changelog-collection step for this plugin
classification_rationale: a cosmetic doc-completeness gap, same class found on 3 sibling branches this run

summary: the plugins\security installer component's description string was not updated when this branch added a fifth DLL to it
trigger: an admin running a custom install and relying on the label to decide what to deploy
classification_rationale: an additive, non-concealing doc-shape gap on a named installer component

summary: the changelog-fragment matcher is blind for every underscore-named plugin fleet-wide (27 plugins verified, not just this one) because every existing fragment filename is hyphenated
trigger: any plugin directory name containing an underscore, matched against the repo's 100%-hyphenated fragment-naming convention
classification_rationale: a pre-existing, systemic generator defect affecting 26 already-shipped plugins identically; not introduced by this branch and not fixable by a per-fragment rename alone

summary: several pure decision functions (decode_mitigation_options, parse_hex_blob, classify_win32_failure, unreadable_failure) lack [[nodiscard]], unlike the sibling Linux/macOS parser header

classification_rationale: a latent hygiene gap with no current caller ignoring the result
